Review – Moa “Southern Alps”

They call it a “White IPA”. Brewed using Nelson Sauvin and citra and fermented using Belgian ale yeast and coriander.

Aroma:

I made the mistake of trying this one straight out of the fridge, which didn’t do it justice initially. After letting it warm up the hop profiles came through and the “IPA” character was evident on the nose. The Belgian yeast gives it the typically spicy aroma which reminded me of Leffe Blonde

Taste:

The Belgian character is at the front and I would classify this as a Belgian ale first and foremost, which was actually a pleasant surprise for me as I had picked it up looking for an IPA flavour. The NZ hops are not overpowering in this and it lets the yeast and high alcohol content do the talking. After a pint I was eager for another right away, which is pretty much the best outcome you can have for a new beer. Being bottle conditioned I made sure to swirl the last dregs into my glass (cloudy beer never scares me), which I would recommend doing.

Avaliability:

In New Zealand pretty much everywhere, I picked it up in New World but I know Pak’n’Save carry it as well and at a good price. The recent sales problems for Moa are being reflected in some good priced beer from them and I will be working my way through their range.

I tried searching online for both UK and USA stockists, no joy. This isn’t Moa’s standard range but strangely no Moa beer showed up in my searches, which is odd as they are a larger player in the New Zealand beer scene. If anyone does know where to pick it up internationally please let me know.
